newsitem.title: GERMANY: German official sees mid-year fall in adj jobless.
newsitem.headline: German official sees mid-year fall in adj jobless.

text.p: The German Labour Office said on Thursday that unemployment could begin to fall on a seasonally-adjusted basis by the middle of the year but that there were few signs of hope for the building sector.

Hans-Peter Leikeb, head of the labour office's jobs market research wing, told Reuters on the sidelines of a news conference that new jobs could come from export-related sectors and a small rise in private consumption.

"Based on the forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth in the government's annual economic report I believe we will see a fall in the seasonally adjusted unemployment jobless figure at the middle of the year," said Leikeb.
"In 1997 the construction sector will not be a source of hope as there are long-term structural changes being made," he added.
German seasonally adjusted unemployment rose 5,000 to 4.316 million in February. On an unadjusted basis, the unemployment rate was 12.2 percent with 4.672 million out of work.
